# Exstream

> Exstream is a JavaScript framework for composable, record-oriented streaming data pipelines in Node.js and modern browsers.

Exstream adapts iterables, async iterables, promises, Node streams, Web Streams, generators, and event sources to one pipeline API. It provides incremental transformations, end-to-end backpressure, bounded asynchronous work, reliable fan-out, streaming formats, record-level error handling, cancellation, and coordinated cleanup.

Use Exstream when a flow must remain bounded, coordinate slow or multiple destinations, or control asynchronous I/O. For small in-memory collections or a simple linear flow, native arrays or `for await` are usually clearer.

## Start here

- [What is Exstream?](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/): framework scope, runtimes, and core pipeline problems
- [Quick start](https://exstream-js.github.io/quick-start/): install Exstream and run a complete streaming pipeline
- [When to use Exstream](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/project/when-not-to-use/): strong use cases, simpler alternatives, and project boundaries
- [Interactive examples](https://exstream-js.github.io/examples/): guided browser-native examples
- [Playground](https://exstream-js.github.io/examples/playground/): edit and run Exstream pipelines in the browser

## Learn

- [Pipeline model](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/pipeline-model/): sources, conversion, merging, transformations, branches, and destinations
- [Create a source](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/sources/): eager and deferred sources, platform streams, generators, promises, and hot events
- [Transform data](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/transform-data/): incremental record operators and reusable transformations
- [Composition](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/composition/): operator functions, `pipeline()`, and `through()`
- [Async processing](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/async-work/): bounded concurrency, ordering, retries, timeouts, throttle, and rate limits
- [Consume a pipeline](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/consume/): laziness, terminal operations, destinations, and readable adapters
- [Backpressure](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/backpressure/): bottlenecks, bounded memory, forks, hot sources, and throttling
- [Fork and observe](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/branching/): reliable branches versus non-blocking observers
- [Merge streams](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/merge/): combine live streams with bounded activation and optional output order
- [Errors and lifecycle](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/errors/): fatal failures, record errors, recovery, retries, dead letters, cancellation, and cleanup
- [Extensibility](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/learn/extensibility/): custom operators, protocol records, context, backpressure, and cleanup

## API reference

- [Complete operator index](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/): every public API grouped by intent
- [`exstream()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/exstream/): create a stream from supported source types or a manual writable source
- [`defer()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/defer/): acquire a source only when the graph starts
- [`fromEvent()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/from-event/): adapt hot EventTarget and EventEmitter sources with explicit overflow behavior
- [`pipeline()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/pipeline/): define reusable typed operator chains
- [`destination()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/destination/): define reusable writers with setup, per-record writes, and cleanup
- [`mapAsync()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/map-async/): asynchronous transformation with concurrency, ordering, retry, recovery, timeout, and cancellation controls
- [`fork()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/fork/): create a reliable branch that participates in backpressure
- [`observe()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/observe/): create a non-blocking observer with explicit buffering
- [`merge()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/merge/): consume a stream of streams with bounded concurrency
- [`through()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/through/): attach a reusable pipeline, operator function, or platform transform
- [Stream state](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/stream-state/): inspect lifecycle, buffering, drops, pressure, and cancellation
- [Error API](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/error-api/): record error metadata, provenance, format errors, overflow, and timeouts
- [`errors()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/errors/): recover, replace, retry, or drop record-level errors
- [`routeErrors()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/route-errors/): route unhandled record errors to a reliable dead-letter branch
- [`csv()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/csv/): incrementally parse CSV across arbitrary chunk boundaries
- [`json()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/json/): incrementally parse one JSON document or top-level array
- [`jsonl()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/jsonl/): parse line-delimited JSON incrementally
- [`pipeTo()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/pipe-to/): run a pipeline into an Exstream, Node, or Web destination
- [Async iteration](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/async-iteration/): consume one value for each `for await` demand
- [Readable and transform interop](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/to-web-readable/): expose Exstream as Web or Node readable streams or as a Node transform
- [`consume()` and `consumeSync()`](https://exstream-js.github.io/docs/reference/consume/): implement low-level custom operators
